title: Export Data Safely
readerIntent: Understand the guarded export boundary and production completion requirements.
priorKnowledge: Know the source schema/service, tenant, allowed fields, format, and destination.
owner: Shared export engine, active format implementation, and governed delivery provider
summary: The current base export service fails closed until an active module supplies source-backed selection, policy-safe rendering, governed delivery, diagnostics, and release evidence.

sections.heading: Intended flow
items: Select an authorized export definition rather than arbitrary source or destination input.
Resolve tenant, source schema/service, allowed query, format, and destination alias.
Apply record and property access policy before data leaves Nodics.
Render through a completed format adapter.
Deliver through a governed provider with timeout, retry, checksum, retention, and cleanup.
Record safe run history and outcome.

sections.heading: Current maturity
paragraphs: CSV, Excel, JSON, and JavaScript-oriented modules provide structure and extension points but must not be described as completed production writers without source-backed behavior and tests. The fail-closed base prevents accidental leakage from partial configuration.

sections.heading: Export scope and policy
items: Authorized model, fields, filters, tenant, catalog, locale, and version.
Stable run identity, format, destination, and checksum.
Maximum records, payload, duration, and concurrency.
Masking, redaction, encryption, retention, and expiry.
Approval and audit for sensitive or bulk data.

sections.heading: Snapshot consistency
paragraphs: The export states whether it represents a transactionally consistent snapshot, a bounded point-in-time view, or a streaming view that may observe concurrent changes.
Search may discover candidates only when permission and freshness are suitable; authoritative services supply protected exported fields.

sections.heading: Destination behavior
items: Write to a governed file, object store, API, or messaging destination adapter.
Use secret references rather than embedded credentials.
Write atomically or publish a completion marker where supported.
Calculate checksum and record size/count.
Clean partial output after failure or retain it as explicitly unusable evidence.

sections.heading: Production gate
items: Source-backed definitions and deterministic rendering.
Tenant, schema, field, and query policy.
Streaming/batching limits and backpressure.
Governed destination aliases and secrets.
Idempotency, retries, partial failure, checksums, retention, and cleanup.
Live delivery, security, performance, recovery, and regression tests.

sections.heading: Verification
items: Allowed and forbidden fields.
Tenant, owner, catalog, and permission isolation.
Empty, small, boundary, and large result sets.
Concurrent data change and declared snapshot behavior.
Destination timeout, partial write, retry, and duplicate request.
Encryption, checksum, expiry, audit, cleanup, and restore.
